title: Reduce launch advisory highlights
summary: Reduce Launch-page yellow advisory rows by treating non-blocking saved-settings notes and inactive ExtraVideoFlags as launch-neutral while preserving highlights for blocked policy contradictions, active raw FFmpeg passthrough, job-failure paths, and safety-gate risks.
reason: Operators read yellow Launch rows as misconfiguration. Normal saved policy choices should not be highlighted unless they can block launch, fail work, or weaken a safety gate.
behavior_before: The Launch settings risk table marked broad review-only settings as yellow, including backend warning counts, media-policy readiness review notes, deferred publish, inactive ExtraVideoFlags under structured presets, H.264 copy tradeoffs, disabled subtitle conversion preferences, PATH fallback, and Validate mode.
behavior_after: The Launch settings risk table keeps normal saved-policy notes ready/neutral. Yellow or blocked rows are reserved for launch-affecting risks such as validation errors, blocked media-policy contradictions, active custom_legacy_flags raw ExtraVideoFlags, strict/fallback size checks, MP4/subtitle container conflicts, source/path readiness gaps, no-audio output, or weakened stability/integrity gates.
tests_added: Added backend policy coverage proving inactive ExtraVideoFlags under balanced_nvenc stay launch-neutral.
Added backend policy coverage proving active custom_legacy_flags raw ExtraVideoFlags still produce Launch review rows.
manual_validation: .\apps\desktop\runtime\Python\python.exe .\ops\scripts\dev\run-python-tool.py mediapipeline.tools.dev.refresh_summaries --paths src/mediapipeline/desktop/application/settings_risk_policy.py - passed, 1 written after final helper cleanup
rollback_plan: Revert the Launch risk handoff and WebView fallback classification changes, restore the prior legacy-flags review assertions, and regenerate the affected summaries.
